text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 26 in history.
1500 - Brazil was discovered by Spanish navigator Vicente Yanes Pinzon.
1788 - The first settlers from England, including a group of convicts, arrived in Sydney, Australia.
1790 - Mozart's opera Cosi Fan Tutte premiered in Vienna.
1802 - The Cisalpine Republic was renamed the Italian Republic with Napoleon Bonaparte as president.
1823 - Edward Jenner, physician, discoverer of vaccination who was in the forefront of the fight against smallpox, died.
1827 - Peru ended its union with Colombia and declared independence.
1837 - Michigan became the 26th U.S. state.
1841 - The British flag was raised on Hong Kong island, six days after China had agreed to cede it to Britain.

1880 - Douglas MacArthur, U.S. army general, born. Supreme Commander of the Allied Forces in the Pacific in World War Two, he accepted the surrender of Japan, carried out a reform programme and gave Japan a new constitution.
1885 - In Sudan, British General Charles Gordon was killed as Khartoum was captured by the Mahdi.
1891 - Nikolaus August Otto, German engineer, developer of the four-stroke internal combustion engine, died.
1905 - The World's largest diamond, the Cullinan, was discovered near Pretoria, weighing 3,106 carats.
1908 - Stephane Grappelli, jazz violinist, born in Paris.
1911 - Richard Strauss's Der Rosenkavalier performed for the first time, in Dresden.
1918 - Nicolae Ceausescu, Romanian head of state, born. Overthrown in a coup in 1989, Ceausescu and his wife Elena were executed by a military firing squad on December 25, 1989.
1925 - Paul Newman, U.S. film actor, born. Nominated for Oscars on several occasions, he finally won one for "The Color of Money" in 1986.
1931 - Mahatma Gandhi was released from prison to hold talks with the government during his civil disobedience campaign.
1936 - In the Spanish Civil War, Franco and his forces captured Barcelona.
1950 - India was formally proclaimed a republic within the Commonwealth.
1965 - The military seized power in South Vietnam, ousting the civilian government of Tran Van Huong.

1965 - Hindi became the official language of India leading to riots in the south of the country. The following month the government announced that English would continue as an associate official language.
1973 - Edward G Robinson, U.S. film actor, died. Most famous for his portrayal of gangsters, Robinson's career was harmed by the McCarthy witchhunts. He received a posthumous Academy Award.
1979 - Nelson Rockefeller, U.S. vice-president to Gerald Ford from 1974-76, died.
1986 - Yoweri Museveni triumphed after a five-year guerrilla war in Uganda against former military ruler Tito Okello.
1991 - Chinese student leader Wang Dan was sentenced to four years in prison for his role in the 1989 pro-democracy movement.
1994 - Boris Fyodorov, the last strong radical in the Russian government, resigned.
1994 - Romania became the first former Cold War foe of NATO to sign a partnership document with the military alliance.
1994 - Media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, one of Italy's richest men, announced that he was entering politics at the head of a "freedom crusade".
1996 - Hillary Rodham Clinton testified before a grand jury investigating the Whitewater affair.
